extra.text: 1.0 PURPOSE The purpose of this report is to summarise the results of Microbial Enumeration Tests, encom- passing Total Aerobic Microbial Count and Total Combined Yeasts and Molds Count, for Sugammadex Sodium manufactured by TEVA, conducted in accordance with the

2.0 SUMMARY Sugammadex Sodium is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin compound used as a selective relax- ant binding agent for the reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuro- nium bromide in adult patients. The drug substance is manufactured by TEVA and is intended for use in the preparation of a sterile injectable drug product.

Microbial Enumeration Tests (MET) for Total Aerobic Microbial Count (TAMC) and Total Yeast and Mold Count (TYMC) are required for Sugammadex Sodium in accordance with Pfizer inter- nal policy standard V7112. As no compendial monograph (USP/EP/BP/JP) mandates a specific microbial limit test for this drug substance, the inclusion of TAMC and TYMC testing is driven by Pfizer policy. The validation was conducted to confirm the suitability of the rinse scheme and membrane filtration method for routine microbial enumeration testing.

The validation was performed at the Chennai Microbiology R&D originating laboratory using three batches of Sugammadex Sodium, in accordance with USP <61> and USP <1227>. The validated method was subsequently transferred to the Rocky Mount, NC QC Microbiology laboratory.

3.0 MICROBIAL ENUMERATION TEST METHOD TRANSFER The Microbial Enumeration Test (MET) validation for Sugammadex Sodium API, manufactured by TEVA, was performed at Chennai R&D Microbiology on three lots of drug substance using the membrane filtration technique with a 0.45 µm mixed cellulose ester membrane. The receiv- ing laboratory for this method transfer is the Rocky Mount, NC QC Microbiology laboratory.

Sample preparation was performed at a 1:10 ratio, comprising 10 g of Sugammadex Sodium drug substance dissolved in 85 mL of sterile phosphate buffer solution pH 7.2, with the addition of 5 mL of 0.1N HCl. Pre-wetting of the membrane filter was performed with an approximate volume of 25 mL Diluting Fluid A (DFA), followed by a rinse scheme of 3×100 mL aliquots of DFA to adequately flush drug substance residues from the filters.
Per SOP-LAB-03312 section 4.2.2, a formal method transfer study is not required for this method because the test method is very similar to the standard test method
The following microorganisms were used as challenge organisms for the validation study.
Per protocol simultaneously, 3 batches method validation and qualification study were executed in triplicates and the results were summarized in this report.
The following sample was taken for validation and Qualification. The drug substance batch de- tails are presented in the table below.
Sample preparation for Microbial Enumeration Test:

Samples of the Sugammadex Sodium drug substances were weighed in separate sterile con- tainers as follows. The sample weights recorded for each container across all three batches are presented in the table below.

The Sugammadex Sodium drug substance solution was prepared at a ratio of 10g of Sugammadex Sodium drug substance in 85 mL of sterile Phosphate Buffer pH 7.2, with the ad- dition of 5 mL of sterile 0.1N HCl. Each sample container was mixed by vortexing until the drug substance was completely dissolved. Following complete dissolution, the obtained solution was filtered through a 0.22 µm filtration system. With this ratio, 10mL of test solution contains ap- proximately 1g of the drug substance.
This 1:10 dilution was termed as Solution-S.
NOTE: Sample solution (1:10) used for Product Negative controls were not sterile filtered as to capture inherit bioburden of the raw material.
3 different Batch number of Sugammadex Sodium Solution-S (10mL) was dispensed sepa- rately, and pH was checked, the observed results were within the acceptance criteria of 6-8.
The pH values recorded for each batch of Sugammadex Sodium are presented in the table below.
5.1.1 Pre-wet three filter membranes with a minimum of 25 mL of Diluting Fluid A and filter the contents.
5.1.2 While the vacuum pump is in the off condition, transfer 10 mL of Solution-S to each filter membrane.

5.1.3 Inoculate the microbial suspension (NMT 100 CFU/0.1 mL) of each challenge microorgan- ism (the volume of the suspension of the inoculum should not be more than 1% of the volume of the diluted product) into the 10 mL of Solution-S and filter the solution. A separate test is re- quired for each microorganism listed in the table of challenge organisms.

5.1.4 RINSE THE FILTERS WITH 3 × 100 ML OF DILUTING FLUID A. 5.1.5 Aseptically transfer the filter membrane containing bacterial cultures onto SCDA plates and incubate at 30–35°C for ≤ 3 days. Repeat steps 5.1.1 to 5.1.4 for yeast and mold cultures and aseptically transfer each filter onto SDA plates and incubate at 20–25°C for ≤ 5 days.
5.1.6 Repeat steps 5.1.1 to 5.1.5 for the remaining two batches of Sugammadex Sodium drug substance.
5.2 PRODUCT NEGATIVE CONTROL The Product Negative Control (PNC) was prepared to confirm the absence of inherent contami- nation in the test material.
5.2.1 Pre-wet three filter membranes with minimum of 25 mL Diluting Fluid A and filter the contents.
5.2.2 Transfer 10 mL of un-filtered sample solution to each filter membrane and filter the con- tents. Rinse the filter with 3 × 100 mL quantity of Diluting Fluid A.
5.2.3 Aseptically transfer the membrane onto SCDA plates and incubate at 30–35°C for NLT 5 days.
5.2.4 Repeat the steps 5.2.1 – 5.2.2 and aseptically transfer the membrane onto SDA plates and incubate at 20–25°C for NLT 7 days.
5.2.5 Repeat the steps 5.2.1 – 5.2.4 for the other 2 batches of Sugammadex Sodium drug sub- stance. Record the results in electronic Lab Notebook (eLN) / Lab notebook.
5.3 BUFFER NEGATIVE CONTROL The Buffer Negative Control was performed to confirm the absence of microbial contamination in the diluent (Phosphate Buffer pH 7.2).
5.3.1 Pre-wet three filter membranes with minimum of 25 mL Diluting Fluid A and filter the contents.
5.3.2 Transfer 10 mL of sterile Phosphate Buffer pH 7.2 to each filter and filter the contents. Rinse the filter with 3 × 100 mL quantity of Diluting Fluid A.

5.3.3 Aseptically transfer the membrane onto SCDA plates and incubate at 30–35°C for NLT 5 days. Repeat steps 5.3.1–5.3.2 and aseptically transfer the membrane onto SDA plates and in- cubate at 20–25°C for NLT 7 days.
5.4 PEPTONE NEGATIVE CONTROL The Peptone Negative Control was performed to confirm the absence of contamination in Diluting Fluid A (DFA).
5.4.1 Pre-wet three filter membranes with a minimum of 25 mL Diluting Fluid A and filter the contents.
5.4.2 Transfer 10 mL of Diluting Fluid A to each filter membrane and filter the contents. Rinse the filters with 3 × 100 mL quantity of Diluting Fluid A.

5.4.3 Aseptically transfer the membrane onto SCDA plates and incubate at 30–35°C for NLT 5 days. Repeat steps 5.4.1 through 5.4.2 and aseptically transfer the membrane onto SDA plates and incubate at 20–25°C for NLT 7 days. Examine plates for the presence or absence of micro- bial growth and record the results in the electronic Lab Notebook (eLN)/Lab notebook.
5.5.1 On the day of the study, the inoculum check was carried out for each microorganism by membrane filtration method.

5.5.2 THREE MEMBRANE FILTERS WERE PRE-WETTED WITH A MINIMUM OF 25 ML DILUTING FLUID A. 5.5.3 While the vacuum pump was in the off condition, 100 mL of Diluting Fluid A was added and the microbial suspension (NMT 100 CFU/0.1 mL) of Bacillus subtilis was inoculated and the solution was filtered.

5.5.4 Steps 5.5.2 to 5.5.3 were repeated for the remaining microorganisms. Filter membranes containing bacterial cultures were aseptically transferred onto SCDA plates and incubated at 30–35°C for NLT 3 days. Filter membranes containing yeast and mold cultures were aseptically transferred onto SDA plates and incubated at 20–25°C for NLT 5 days.

5.6 RESULTS The Microbial Enumeration Test validation was conducted on three batches of Sugammadex Sodium using Soybean Casein Digest Agar (SCDA) plates for bacterial enumeration and Sabouraud Dextrose Agar (SDA) plates for yeast and mold enumeration. Product Positive Control (PPC) and Inoculum Count (IC) plates were evaluated for all five challenge microorgan- isms across all three batches. The percentage recovery for each microorganism was calculated using the formula: % Recovery = (Average PPC / Average IC) × 100.

From the data presented above, it is observed that the percentage recovery values for all chal- lenge microorganisms across all three batches were within the acceptance criteria of ≥50% and ≤200%, when compared against the respective Inoculum Count (IC) verification plates. The colony morphology observed on PPC plates was found to be consistent with the respective challenge microorganisms.
► Equivalency percentage Recovery Calculation for mold & yeast between SCDA of PPC plate vs SDA of IC Plate:

For Aspergillus brasiliensis and Candida albicans, the PPC plates were prepared on both SCDA and SDA media, and the IC plates were prepared on SDA media. The equivalency re- covery comparison between PPC on SCDA and IC on SDA was performed to assess the suit- ability of using SCDA alone for routine bioburden testing.

The equivalency recovery values for Aspergillus brasiliensis and Candida albicans, comparing PPC on SCDA against IC on SDA, were found to comply with the acceptance criteria of ≥50% and ≤200% for all three batches.

8.0 CONCLUSION Three batches of Sugammadex Sodium were evaluated for Microbial Enumeration Tests (TAMC and TYMC) as part of method validation and transfer to Rocky Mount, NC. The recovery of each microorganism in the Product Positive Control (PPC) was found to be between 50% and 200% when compared against the Inoculum Count (IC) verification for all three batches. All results met the predefined validity and acceptance criteria; on the basis of the data generated, it is concluded that the method is suitable for routine analysis.
Summary Report for Validation and Transfer of Microbial Enumeration Tests of Sugammadex Sodium to Rocky Mount, NC

For Aspergillus brasiliensis and Candida albicans, the comparison between PPC on SCDA and IC on SDA met the acceptance criteria of ≥50% and ≤200%, thereby demonstrating equiva- lency between SCDA and SDA for the growth of yeasts and molds. It is therefore concluded that the routine bioburden test may be performed using SCDA media only, at incubation condi- tions of 30–35°C for not less than (NLT) 3 days.
